**Kim Bendix Petersen** (born 14 June 1956),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-bio-1) better known by his stage name **King Diamond**, is a Danish rock musician. As a vocalist, he is known for his powerful and wide-ranging countertenor singing voice, in particular his far-reaching falsetto screams. He is the lead vocalist and lyricist for both Mercyful Fate and the eponymous King Diamond. He also plays keyboards and guitars on studio recordings but uses live shows to focus solely on his vocal performance. Diamond is renowned for his dark lyrical content and his story concepts. He is also known for his distinctive shock stage persona (in particular his black and white facepaint). He has been an influence for other rock and metal artists, including Metallica,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto-3)Slayer[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-Metal_Hammer-4) and Cradle of Filth.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto1-5).

Kim Petersen was born in Hvidovre, a suburb of Copenhagen, Denmark on June 14, 1956. His father worked as a foreman at a storage facility, while his mother was secretary to the city's mayor. He grew up alongside his younger brother Stig. He revealed that growing up there was strict discipline in the way he and his brother were raised but lived a "very normal childhood." Petersen first became curious about occultism after listening to Black Sabbath and reading about Jimmy Page's interest in Aleister Crowley. These interests eventually led to him reading the work of Anton LaVey.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-6)
He attended basic school for 10 years and then attended college, where studied to become a lab assistant. By this time he was playing music but mostly as a hobby.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7)
King Diamond's first heavy rock band was called Brainstorm (1974–76), with Jeanette Blum (Jean Blue) on vocals and bass, Michael Frohn (Mike West) on guitar and Jes Jacobsen (Jesse James) on drums. Diamond left Brainstorm and began singing with local Danish hard rock band Black Rose. He began experimenting with horror-themed theatrics and shaping a malevolent quasi-Satanic stage persona. He left Black Rose and joined the punk-metal band Brats, where he met Hank Shermann. The two were soon asked to help Michael Denner (also formerly a member of Brats) with his own project, Danger Zone. This band included Timi Hansen, and the musicians would join with Diamond in 1980 to become Mercyful Fate.
When Diamond first started Mercyful Fate, the band was not making much money and was taking up a lot of his time. Eventually, he decided to quit his job and live off of social security in order to focus on the band. Not long afterward, however, Mercyful Fate began to take off.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7)

Following Mercyful Fate's 1984 release of _[Don't Break the Oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Break\_the\_Oath "Don't Break the Oath")_ and the subsequent tour (which saw them play in the U.S. for the first time), Diamond split ways with Mercyful Fate. With him, he took two of his bandmates (Hansen and Denner) to pursue a solo career under his own name.
Mercyful Fate reunited in 1992 (while Diamond simultaneously continued his solo career) and recorded five more studio albums. In 1999, Diamond and Hank Shermann performed the song "Evil" live with Metallica. This performance also featured Diamond without his famous makeup.
King Diamond in 1999
In 2000, Diamond decided to put Mercyful Fate on hold and continue on with his solo career.
On 1 August 2019, Mercyful Fate announced a reunion and an accompanying European tour.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-8) On 2 June 2022, Mercyful Fate performed their first live show since 1999 in Hanover as part of a European tour, where they debuted a brand new song titled "The Jackal of Salzbur." King Diamond also confirmed that the band was actively working on a new album.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-10) However, in January 2025 the band's bass player, Becky Baldwin, stated that the new Mercyful Fate album was not expected to be released before 2025, due to King Diamond's focus on his namesake band's upcoming thirteenth studio album.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-11)

After Mercyful Fate broke up, King Diamond, along with Michael Denner and Timi Hansen, formed the eponymous King Diamond band in 1985.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-12)_Fatal Portrait_, the band's first full-length studio album, was released on 14 March 1986, through Roadrunner Records.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-13) Their second album _Abigail_, was released on 29 May 1987 was the first concept album based on an original story by Diamond.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-14) Following some line up changes another concept album, _"Them"_ charted at number 38 on the Swedish album chart, number 65 on the Dutch album chart, and at number 89 on the _Billboard_ 200, making it King Diamond's highest charting album in the U.S. to date.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-16) Diamonds album a continuation of the storyline from _"Them"_, _Conspiracy_ was the first King Diamond album to be recorded in the United States and was released in 1989.

The next album _The Eye_ was released the following year in 1990, however King Diamond reunited with Mercyful Fate in 1992 where he would then balance recording and touring with both Mercyful Fate and his eponymous band throughout the 1990s.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-18) After recording and touring with Mercyful Fate, King Diamond reformed his eponymous band in 1994.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-19) Released on 1 October 1996, _The Graveyard_ saw King Diamond return to writing concept albums this was then followed by 1998 _Voodoo._[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-20) Then when Mercyful Fate was put on hold in 1999, King Diamond began recording the album _House of God_ at the Nomad Recording Studio in Carrollton, Texas.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-21)
In 2001, King Diamond worked out a deal with the band Usurper to sing backup vocals on the song "Necronemesis" in exchange for them shifting their recording schedule around to accommodate the recording of _Abigail II: The Revenge_. In 2003 King Diamond released their eleventh album _The Puppet Master_, the album also featured additional vocals from Diamond's wife Livia Zita.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-22) In 2004, Diamond contributed vocals to "Sweet Dreams", the final track on the album of Dave Grohl's heavy metal side project Probot. In late 2005, Diamond appeared on the _Roadrunner United – The All-Star Sessions_ album, contributing vocals for his song "In the Fire", which featured multiple Roadrunner Records musicians (past and present) working together to create individual songs. Diamond also guested on the Cradle of Filth song "Devil Woman" in late 2005.

In April 2006, Diamond reunited with Mikkey Dee (Motörhead drummer) at a sold-out gig at Kåren in Gothenburg, Sweden.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-23) In 2001 he referred to Dee as "one of the best drummers of all time and that's something that has bothered us since he left."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-24)
Diamond released his album _Give Me Your Soul... Please_, on 26 June 2007. The band received a Grammy nomination in the "Best Metal Performance" category for the track "Never Ending Hill".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-Blabbermouth.net-25)
He was forced to cancel a United States tour due to a herniated disk, causing severe back pain, which puts him in intense pain almost all of the time.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-26) He attributes the problem to the long stressful hours spent working on the album.
Diamond made an appearance at Ozzfest on 9 August 2008 at Frisco, Texas alongside Metallica, performing a medley of Mercyful Fate songs previously released on Metallica's _[Garage Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garage\_Inc. "Garage Inc.")_ album. He also performed a cover of the Pantera song "A New Level" with Vinnie Paul, Scott Ian, Max Cavalera, and Nick Bowcott.
In 2009, Diamond was revealed to be a playable character for the rhythm game_Guitar Hero: Metallica_, appearing with Mercyful Fate's song "Evil". The player must complete the song on any instrument and any difficulty to unlock the character.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-27)

On 29 November 2010, Diamond was taken to the hospital, where doctors discovered several blockages in his arteries due to his heavy smoking habit. They determined that he had had several heart attacks and that he needed triple-bypass surgery, during which time he was medically dead for five hours.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-28) The surgery was performed successfully and on 11 December 2010 it was announced that he was at home recovering.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-29) All his musical projects were placed on hold.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-30)
On 7 December 2011, Diamond appeared on stage with Metallica at the Fillmore in San Francisco to celebrate Metallica's 30th anniversary.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-31)
In June 2012, Diamond performed his comeback concert at Sweden Rock Festival.
On Saturday 8 September 2012, Diamond appeared along with Mark Tremonti on VH1 Classic's _That Metal Show_ discussing his surgery and various details about upcoming events.
King Diamond in 2013
He appeared on Volbeat's 2013 album, _Outlaw Gentlemen & Shady Ladies_, providing guest vocals on the track "Room 24".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-32) This collaboration resulted in another Grammy nomination for Best Metal Performance at the 56th Annual Grammy Awards.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:0-33) In August 2013 Diamond performed at Open Air Bloodstock Festival, UK.
Slayer was chosen to headline the 2015 Rockstar Energy Mayhem Festival. The bands HELLYEAH, King Diamond, The Devil Wears Prada, Thy Art Is Murder, Jungle Rot, Sister Sin, Sworn In, Shattered Sun, Feed Her To The Sharks, Code Orange and Kissing Candice also participated in the Rockstar Tour.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-34)

In 2018, King Diamond began work on its thirteenth studio album, which would be divided into two parts to connect with its theme. The first part of the series was later revealed to be titled _The Institute_; the title has since been changed to _Saint Lucifer's Hospital 1920_. Originally intended for release in 2020, it faced multiple delays before its planned release in 2026. This delay was in part due to Diamond taking his time on perfecting new material by both the King Diamond band and the reunited Mercyful Fate.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-36)
In the spring and summer of 2025, King Diamond toured Europe, bringing along Paradise Lost, Angel Witch and Unto Others.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-37) In November of 2025 Diamond was honored by the Danish Arts Foundation and was given the lifetime honour for his "very special efforts and contributions to Danish art and cultural life." In addition Diamond will receive a yearly 189,000 Danish Krona (about $26,000) grant from the foundation for the rest of his life.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:1-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-39)
On September 12, 2026, Diamond joined My Chemical Romance on stage at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas to perform the song "Mama".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-40)
Diamond was a special celebrity guest star in four episodes of the [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") adult-oriented cartoon _Metalocalypse_ as the Blues Devil, Ronald von Moldenberg, a fast food manager, and one of the Klokateers in 2006 on Adult Swim.
Diamond performing in Ballenstedt, Germany in 2025

Diamond is known for his multi-octave vocal range, in particular his far reaching and stable tone when singing in falsetto.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-41)_Revolver_ wrote "the Danish metal royal has commanded our attention through Satan-summoning performances, demonic grunting and a glass-shattering falsetto that’s part Maria Callas, part Rob Halford and completely jaw-dropping."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-42)
He is known for creating conceptual works that feature recurring stories that include the supernatural, horror, fate and death. His lyrics have been described as a "gothic horror romance in metal form, delivered with technical precision and theatrical grandeur."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:1-38) Diamond has stated he has loved of horror films since his youth when he would watch _Frankenstein_ and _Dracula_ with his parents; these films have also played a part in his lyrical style.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7) Diamond said that when he first joined Mercyful Fate, he lived in a apartment that "turned out to be truly haunted." He stated in an interview with Blabbermouth.net: "Many of the things that are written in the lyrics have been taken straight as they happened from these real experiences."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7) In that same interview, he stated that a lot of his lyrics are drawn from real life, but some come from his imagination: "To make a story flow, you change some of the things that you've experienced. When an album is done and I read through all the lyrics, I get a little uneasy when I see how much of myself I've put into the stories. But then again, I know that no one's going to know unless I tell them exactly what's what, and I'm certainly not going to do that. But it's drawn from everywhere."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7)

Diamond cites Arthur Brown, David Byron, Alice Cooper, Ronnie James Dio, Ian Gillan, Ozzy Osbourne and Robert Plant as his primary influences. According to Diamond's biography on his official website, the first two albums he bought were Deep Purple's _Fireball_ and Black Sabbath's _Master of Reality_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-43)
On stage, Diamond uses a microphone stand consisting of a femur bone and a tibia bone in the shape of a cross. He previously used a human skull, called Melissa, on stage. In the mid-1980s Melissa was stolen after a performance in the Netherlands._[citation needed_] Diamond is also known for his Corpse paint and has changed the design of his make-up often over the years. With _Conspiracy_, he wore a mesh of black and white line war paint, with some red "blood" made to look like a wound coming out of his forehead. With his album _The Puppet Master_, he used very little white and mainly had black crosses and inverted crosses going up and down his face.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-44) Diamond is also known for his onstage performance. _Brave Worlds_ described his stage presence stating "On stage, he transforms the concert into a dark theatre – a ritual where gothic tales, horrific characters and symbolic scenography merge. His distinctive "corpsepaint" and his microphone holder, an inverted cross made of human bones, make him an iconic figure."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:1-38)

Diamond is married to Livia Zita, a Hungarian-born singer who has made appearances as a backup vocalist on the albums _The Puppet Master_ and _Give Me Your Soul...Please_, as well as during live performances. She is also his business partner, and is currently_[when?_] working with him to compile old footage for two planned DVD releases of King Diamond and Mercyful Fate live performances. She also helped him make remastered editions of the King Diamond albums _[The Spider's Lullabye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Spider's\_Lullabye "The Spider's Lullabye")_, _The Graveyard_, _Voodoo_ and _House of God_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-45) In 2017, they became parents to a son,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-46) born in March.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-48) In a 2016 interview with _Metal Hammer_ Diamond revealed that following his health scare he has given up smoking and started living a healthier life style, which he has credited to helping improve his singing voice.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49) Some of Diamonds interest include Formula One and Football, growing up he played for the youth squad of Danish club called Hvidovre IF but he stopped playing once he went to college and started getting involved in music.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-50)
Although he was born and raised in Denmark, Diamond relocated to Dallas / Fort Worth, Texas in the 1980s.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-51) In 2010, Diamond officially quit smoking following his triple-bypass-surgery.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49)

Diamond followsLaVeyan Satanism, which he does not see as a religion, but a philosophy by which he lived even before reading occultistAnton LaVey's _The Satanic Bible_.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-rhi1-52)Michael Moynihan calls him "one of the only performers of the '80s Satanic Metal who was more than just a poseur using a devilish image for shock value".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-loc15f-53) Diamond has expressed concern that religion has led so many people to kill and destroy each other. He stated that he cannot comprehend why religion has caused so much death and destruction when it is logically impossible to prove the presence or absence of any deity. He states that he has reached a point in his life where he has completely given up believing in anything religious.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-54) Despite being non religious Diamond revealed in a 2016, interview with _Metal Hammer_ that he is "very spiritual."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49)
Metallica released an 11-minute medley of five Mercyful Fate songs on their 1998 _[Garage Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garage\_Inc. "Garage Inc.")_ cover album. King Diamond has provided guest vocals for live performances of the medley at Metallica's concerts on three occasions: at the 1999 Gods of Metal festival in Milan, Italy (with Hank Shermann on guitar);[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-55) at the 2008 Ozzfest in Dallas, Texas;[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-56) and at a 2011 Metallica fan club gig in San Francisco, California (with Hank Shermann on guitar, Michael Denner on guitar and Timi Hansen on bass).[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-GWorld-57)

King Diamond has appeared on the covers of many rock and metal magazines, and has influenced many artists, including Metallica's Lars Ulrich,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto-3)Cradle of Filth,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto1-5)Cage,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-58) and Andy DiGelsomina of the Wagnerian opera metal project Lyraka.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-59)
American heavy metal band Cage devoted to him the song "King Diamond" on the album _Hell Destroyer_ in 2007.
In 2006, Diamond was ranked at number 85 in _Hit Parader's_ "Top 100 Metal Vocalists of All Time".[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-60) In 2016 he was ranked number 38 on _Loudwire_’s list of the 66 Best Hard Rock and Metal Frontman of All Time.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-61)
King Diamond has inspired many bands; Metallica,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-62)Slayer,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-63)Opeth,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-64)Pantera,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-65)Cradle of Filth[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto1-5) and Emperor[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-66) have all cited him as a influence.

**Kim Bendix Petersen** (born 14 June 1956),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-bio-1) better known by his stage name **King Diamond**, is a Danish rock musician. As a vocalist, he is known for his powerful and wide-ranging countertenor singing voice, in particular his far-reaching falsetto screams. He is the lead vocalist and lyricist for both Mercyful Fate and the eponymous King Diamond. He also plays keyboards and guitars on studio recordings but uses live shows to focus solely on his vocal performance. Diamond is renowned for his dark lyrical content and his story concepts. He is also known for his distinctive shock stage persona (in particular his black and white facepaint). He has been an influence for other rock and metal artists, including Metallica,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto-3)Slayer[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-Metal_Hammer-4) and Cradle of Filth.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto1-5).
texts.1:
Kim Petersen was born in Hvidovre, a suburb of Copenhagen, Denmark on June 14, 1956. His father worked as a foreman at a storage facility, while his mother was secretary to the city's mayor. He grew up alongside his younger brother Stig. He revealed that growing up there was strict discipline in the way he and his brother were raised but lived a "very normal childhood." Petersen first became curious about occultism after listening to Black Sabbath and reading about Jimmy Page's interest in Aleister Crowley. These interests eventually led to him reading the work of Anton LaVey.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-6)
He attended basic school for 10 years and then attended college, where studied to become a lab assistant. By this time he was playing music but mostly as a hobby.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7)
King Diamond's first heavy rock band was called Brainstorm (1974–76), with Jeanette Blum (Jean Blue) on vocals and bass, Michael Frohn (Mike West) on guitar and Jes Jacobsen (Jesse James) on drums. Diamond left Brainstorm and began singing with local Danish hard rock band Black Rose. He began experimenting with horror-themed theatrics and shaping a malevolent quasi-Satanic stage persona. He left Black Rose and joined the punk-metal band Brats, where he met Hank Shermann. The two were soon asked to help Michael Denner (also formerly a member of Brats) with his own project, Danger Zone. This band included Timi Hansen, and the musicians would join with Diamond in 1980 to become Mercyful Fate.
When Diamond first started Mercyful Fate, the band was not making much money and was taking up a lot of his time. Eventually, he decided to quit his job and live off of social security in order to focus on the band. Not long afterward, however, Mercyful Fate began to take off.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7)
texts.2:
Following Mercyful Fate's 1984 release of _[Don't Break the Oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Break\_the\_Oath "Don't Break the Oath")_ and the subsequent tour (which saw them play in the U.S. for the first time), Diamond split ways with Mercyful Fate. With him, he took two of his bandmates (Hansen and Denner) to pursue a solo career under his own name.
Mercyful Fate reunited in 1992 (while Diamond simultaneously continued his solo career) and recorded five more studio albums. In 1999, Diamond and Hank Shermann performed the song "Evil" live with Metallica. This performance also featured Diamond without his famous makeup.
King Diamond in 1999
In 2000, Diamond decided to put Mercyful Fate on hold and continue on with his solo career.
On 1 August 2019, Mercyful Fate announced a reunion and an accompanying European tour.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-8) On 2 June 2022, Mercyful Fate performed their first live show since 1999 in Hanover as part of a European tour, where they debuted a brand new song titled "The Jackal of Salzbur." King Diamond also confirmed that the band was actively working on a new album.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-10) However, in January 2025 the band's bass player, Becky Baldwin, stated that the new Mercyful Fate album was not expected to be released before 2025, due to King Diamond's focus on his namesake band's upcoming thirteenth studio album.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-11)
texts.3: After Mercyful Fate broke up, King Diamond, along with Michael Denner and Timi Hansen, formed the eponymous King Diamond band in 1985.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-12)_Fatal Portrait_, the band's first full-length studio album, was released on 14 March 1986, through Roadrunner Records.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-13) Their second album _Abigail_, was released on 29 May 1987 was the first concept album based on an original story by Diamond.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-14) Following some line up changes another concept album, _"Them"_ charted at number 38 on the Swedish album chart, number 65 on the Dutch album chart, and at number 89 on the _Billboard_ 200, making it King Diamond's highest charting album in the U.S. to date.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-16) Diamonds album a continuation of the storyline from _"Them"_, _Conspiracy_ was the first King Diamond album to be recorded in the United States and was released in 1989.
texts.4:
The next album _The Eye_ was released the following year in 1990, however King Diamond reunited with Mercyful Fate in 1992 where he would then balance recording and touring with both Mercyful Fate and his eponymous band throughout the 1990s.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-18) After recording and touring with Mercyful Fate, King Diamond reformed his eponymous band in 1994.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-19) Released on 1 October 1996, _The Graveyard_ saw King Diamond return to writing concept albums this was then followed by 1998 _Voodoo._[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-20) Then when Mercyful Fate was put on hold in 1999, King Diamond began recording the album _House of God_ at the Nomad Recording Studio in Carrollton, Texas.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-21)
In 2001, King Diamond worked out a deal with the band Usurper to sing backup vocals on the song "Necronemesis" in exchange for them shifting their recording schedule around to accommodate the recording of _Abigail II: The Revenge_. In 2003 King Diamond released their eleventh album _The Puppet Master_, the album also featured additional vocals from Diamond's wife Livia Zita.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-22) In 2004, Diamond contributed vocals to "Sweet Dreams", the final track on the album of Dave Grohl's heavy metal side project Probot. In late 2005, Diamond appeared on the _Roadrunner United – The All-Star Sessions_ album, contributing vocals for his song "In the Fire", which featured multiple Roadrunner Records musicians (past and present) working together to create individual songs. Diamond also guested on the Cradle of Filth song "Devil Woman" in late 2005.
texts.5:
In April 2006, Diamond reunited with Mikkey Dee (Motörhead drummer) at a sold-out gig at Kåren in Gothenburg, Sweden.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-23) In 2001 he referred to Dee as "one of the best drummers of all time and that's something that has bothered us since he left."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-24)
Diamond released his album _Give Me Your Soul... Please_, on 26 June 2007. The band received a Grammy nomination in the "Best Metal Performance" category for the track "Never Ending Hill".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-Blabbermouth.net-25)
He was forced to cancel a United States tour due to a herniated disk, causing severe back pain, which puts him in intense pain almost all of the time.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-26) He attributes the problem to the long stressful hours spent working on the album.
Diamond made an appearance at Ozzfest on 9 August 2008 at Frisco, Texas alongside Metallica, performing a medley of Mercyful Fate songs previously released on Metallica's _[Garage Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garage\_Inc. "Garage Inc.")_ album. He also performed a cover of the Pantera song "A New Level" with Vinnie Paul, Scott Ian, Max Cavalera, and Nick Bowcott.
In 2009, Diamond was revealed to be a playable character for the rhythm game_Guitar Hero: Metallica_, appearing with Mercyful Fate's song "Evil". The player must complete the song on any instrument and any difficulty to unlock the character.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-27)
texts.6:
On 29 November 2010, Diamond was taken to the hospital, where doctors discovered several blockages in his arteries due to his heavy smoking habit. They determined that he had had several heart attacks and that he needed triple-bypass surgery, during which time he was medically dead for five hours.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-28) The surgery was performed successfully and on 11 December 2010 it was announced that he was at home recovering.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-29) All his musical projects were placed on hold.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-30)
On 7 December 2011, Diamond appeared on stage with Metallica at the Fillmore in San Francisco to celebrate Metallica's 30th anniversary.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-31)
In June 2012, Diamond performed his comeback concert at Sweden Rock Festival.
On Saturday 8 September 2012, Diamond appeared along with Mark Tremonti on VH1 Classic's _That Metal Show_ discussing his surgery and various details about upcoming events.
King Diamond in 2013
He appeared on Volbeat's 2013 album, _Outlaw Gentlemen & Shady Ladies_, providing guest vocals on the track "Room 24".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-32) This collaboration resulted in another Grammy nomination for Best Metal Performance at the 56th Annual Grammy Awards.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:0-33) In August 2013 Diamond performed at Open Air Bloodstock Festival, UK.
Slayer was chosen to headline the 2015 Rockstar Energy Mayhem Festival. The bands HELLYEAH, King Diamond, The Devil Wears Prada, Thy Art Is Murder, Jungle Rot, Sister Sin, Sworn In, Shattered Sun, Feed Her To The Sharks, Code Orange and Kissing Candice also participated in the Rockstar Tour.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-34)
texts.7:
In 2018, King Diamond began work on its thirteenth studio album, which would be divided into two parts to connect with its theme. The first part of the series was later revealed to be titled _The Institute_; the title has since been changed to _Saint Lucifer's Hospital 1920_. Originally intended for release in 2020, it faced multiple delays before its planned release in 2026. This delay was in part due to Diamond taking his time on perfecting new material by both the King Diamond band and the reunited Mercyful Fate.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-36)
In the spring and summer of 2025, King Diamond toured Europe, bringing along Paradise Lost, Angel Witch and Unto Others.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-37) In November of 2025 Diamond was honored by the Danish Arts Foundation and was given the lifetime honour for his "very special efforts and contributions to Danish art and cultural life." In addition Diamond will receive a yearly 189,000 Danish Krona (about $26,000) grant from the foundation for the rest of his life.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:1-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-39)
On September 12, 2026, Diamond joined My Chemical Romance on stage at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas to perform the song "Mama".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-40)
Diamond was a special celebrity guest star in four episodes of the [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") adult-oriented cartoon _Metalocalypse_ as the Blues Devil, Ronald von Moldenberg, a fast food manager, and one of the Klokateers in 2006 on Adult Swim.
Diamond performing in Ballenstedt, Germany in 2025
texts.8:
Diamond is known for his multi-octave vocal range, in particular his far reaching and stable tone when singing in falsetto.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-41)_Revolver_ wrote "the Danish metal royal has commanded our attention through Satan-summoning performances, demonic grunting and a glass-shattering falsetto that’s part Maria Callas, part Rob Halford and completely jaw-dropping."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-42)
He is known for creating conceptual works that feature recurring stories that include the supernatural, horror, fate and death. His lyrics have been described as a "gothic horror romance in metal form, delivered with technical precision and theatrical grandeur."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:1-38) Diamond has stated he has loved of horror films since his youth when he would watch _Frankenstein_ and _Dracula_ with his parents; these films have also played a part in his lyrical style.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7) Diamond said that when he first joined Mercyful Fate, he lived in a apartment that "turned out to be truly haunted." He stated in an interview with Blabbermouth.net: "Many of the things that are written in the lyrics have been taken straight as they happened from these real experiences."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7) In that same interview, he stated that a lot of his lyrics are drawn from real life, but some come from his imagination: "To make a story flow, you change some of the things that you've experienced. When an album is done and I read through all the lyrics, I get a little uneasy when I see how much of myself I've put into the stories. But then again, I know that no one's going to know unless I tell them exactly what's what, and I'm certainly not going to do that. But it's drawn from everywhere."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7)
texts.9:
Diamond cites Arthur Brown, David Byron, Alice Cooper, Ronnie James Dio, Ian Gillan, Ozzy Osbourne and Robert Plant as his primary influences. According to Diamond's biography on his official website, the first two albums he bought were Deep Purple's _Fireball_ and Black Sabbath's _Master of Reality_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-43)
On stage, Diamond uses a microphone stand consisting of a femur bone and a tibia bone in the shape of a cross. He previously used a human skull, called Melissa, on stage. In the mid-1980s Melissa was stolen after a performance in the Netherlands._[citation needed_] Diamond is also known for his Corpse paint and has changed the design of his make-up often over the years. With _Conspiracy_, he wore a mesh of black and white line war paint, with some red "blood" made to look like a wound coming out of his forehead. With his album _The Puppet Master_, he used very little white and mainly had black crosses and inverted crosses going up and down his face.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-44) Diamond is also known for his onstage performance. _Brave Worlds_ described his stage presence stating "On stage, he transforms the concert into a dark theatre – a ritual where gothic tales, horrific characters and symbolic scenography merge. His distinctive "corpsepaint" and his microphone holder, an inverted cross made of human bones, make him an iconic figure."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:1-38)
texts.10:
Diamond is married to Livia Zita, a Hungarian-born singer who has made appearances as a backup vocalist on the albums _The Puppet Master_ and _Give Me Your Soul...Please_, as well as during live performances. She is also his business partner, and is currently_[when?_] working with him to compile old footage for two planned DVD releases of King Diamond and Mercyful Fate live performances. She also helped him make remastered editions of the King Diamond albums _[The Spider's Lullabye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Spider's\_Lullabye "The Spider's Lullabye")_, _The Graveyard_, _Voodoo_ and _House of God_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-45) In 2017, they became parents to a son,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-46) born in March.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-48) In a 2016 interview with _Metal Hammer_ Diamond revealed that following his health scare he has given up smoking and started living a healthier life style, which he has credited to helping improve his singing voice.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49) Some of Diamonds interest include Formula One and Football, growing up he played for the youth squad of Danish club called Hvidovre IF but he stopped playing once he went to college and started getting involved in music.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-50)
Although he was born and raised in Denmark, Diamond relocated to Dallas / Fort Worth, Texas in the 1980s.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-51) In 2010, Diamond officially quit smoking following his triple-bypass-surgery.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49)
texts.11:
Diamond followsLaVeyan Satanism, which he does not see as a religion, but a philosophy by which he lived even before reading occultistAnton LaVey's _The Satanic Bible_.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-rhi1-52)Michael Moynihan calls him "one of the only performers of the '80s Satanic Metal who was more than just a poseur using a devilish image for shock value".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-loc15f-53) Diamond has expressed concern that religion has led so many people to kill and destroy each other. He stated that he cannot comprehend why religion has caused so much death and destruction when it is logically impossible to prove the presence or absence of any deity. He states that he has reached a point in his life where he has completely given up believing in anything religious.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-54) Despite being non religious Diamond revealed in a 2016, interview with _Metal Hammer_ that he is "very spiritual."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49)
Metallica released an 11-minute medley of five Mercyful Fate songs on their 1998 _[Garage Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garage\_Inc. "Garage Inc.")_ cover album. King Diamond has provided guest vocals for live performances of the medley at Metallica's concerts on three occasions: at the 1999 Gods of Metal festival in Milan, Italy (with Hank Shermann on guitar);[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-55) at the 2008 Ozzfest in Dallas, Texas;[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-56) and at a 2011 Metallica fan club gig in San Francisco, California (with Hank Shermann on guitar, Michael Denner on guitar and Timi Hansen on bass).[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-GWorld-57)
texts.12:
King Diamond has appeared on the covers of many rock and metal magazines, and has influenced many artists, including Metallica's Lars Ulrich,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto-3)Cradle of Filth,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto1-5)Cage,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-58) and Andy DiGelsomina of the Wagnerian opera metal project Lyraka.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-59)
American heavy metal band Cage devoted to him the song "King Diamond" on the album _Hell Destroyer_ in 2007.
In 2006, Diamond was ranked at number 85 in _Hit Parader's_ "Top 100 Metal Vocalists of All Time".[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-60) In 2016 he was ranked number 38 on _Loudwire_’s list of the 66 Best Hard Rock and Metal Frontman of All Time.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-61)
King Diamond has inspired many bands; Metallica,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-62)Slayer,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-63)Opeth,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-64)Pantera,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-65)Cradle of Filth[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto1-5) and Emperor[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-66) have all cited him as a influence.

Mercyful Fate was formed in early 1981 in Copenhagen, Denmark, by vocalist King Diamond and guitar player Hank Shermann. Guitarist Michael Denner, Bassist Timi Hansen and drummer Kim Ruzz soon joined to complete the band line-up.
The band recorded two demos in 1981, and later signed with Rave On Records in Holland, for recording of their successful EP “Mercyful Fate”, released on November 8th 1982. The EP was soon in heavy rotation around the core metal radio stations, starting a new breed in Heavy Metal with their unique sound.
Mercyful Fate signed a new deal with Roadrunner Records in 1983 to make their first full length album “Melissa”, recorded and released that same year. In 1984 the band went back into the studio to record their legendary album “Don’t Break The Oath”, released on September 7th 1984.
Soon after Mercyful Fate started a two month US Tour, which took them across the States several times, including sharing the stage with Motorhead and Exciter for the last part of the tour. The shows had created a brush fire within the metal community, and Mercyful Fate was now getting a lot of recognition. The year of 1984 ended with a 5 days tour in Germany, together with Motorhead, Girlschool, Helix and Talon.
First concert of 1985 was in their hometown of Copenhagen, an old movie theater with higher capacity. The show was sold out, and the band displayed new levels of their stage show. It was a huge success, and was a new highlight for Mercyful Fate.
In April 1985 though, the band decided to part ways, for each to pursue new challenges. The King Diamond band was born and had huge success the following years with five studio album releases on Roadrunner Records. King Diamond has since signed with Metal Blade Records, and is going stronger than ever.
Summer of 1992 Mercyful Fate decided to get back together and penned a new deal with Brian Slagel and his label Metal Blade Records. “In The Shadows” was released in 1993, and was and instant success followed by a sold out US tour.

The following years Mercyful Fate released another five studio albums and toured Europe, US and South America many times. The highlight of the year 1999 was their critically acclaimed “9” album, released on May 25th 1999. It was followed by a European tour with Metallica, where King and Hank several times joined them on stage performing the medley “Mercyful Fate” which Metallica had recorded on their “Garage Inc.” double tribute album, in 1998. A USA tour and touring in South America followed.
Mercyful Fate played 36 concerts in Europe, USA and Mexico in 2022. Two concerts in South America in 2024. Work in progress for a full Album.

**Mercyful Fate** is a Danish heavy metal band from Copenhagen, formed in 1981 by vocalist King Diamond and guitarist Hank Shermann.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-shermann_bio-2) Influenced by progressive rock and hard rock, and with lyrics dealing with LaVeyan Satanism (often with ironic or sardonic use of Christian themes) and the occult, Mercyful Fate was part of the first wave of black metal in the early to mid-1980s, along with Venom and Bathory.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-4) The band is also cited as a formative influence to the then-nascent genres of thrash metal[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Kerry_King-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-metalinjection-6) and death metal, as well as the Norwegian black metal scene.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Melissa_Review-9)

Since its inception in 1981, Mercyful Fate has released seven studio albums, two extended plays, and four compilation albums. After several line-up changes and self-made demos, they released their self-titled EP in 1982, with the line-up of King Diamond (vocals), Hank Shermann (lead and rhythm guitars), Michael Denner (rhythm and lead guitars), Timi Hansen (bass), and Kim Ruzz (drums). With this line-up, the group recorded its first two studio albums: 1983's _Melissa_ and 1984's _[Don't Break the Oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Break\_the\_Oath "Don't Break the Oath")_. In spite of their reputation as one of the most acclaimed bands of the European heavy metal scene of the 1980s, Mercyful Fate was the subject of controversy due to their satanic imagery, and one of their songs "Into the Coven" (from _Melissa_) later gained notoriety for appearing as one of the PMRC's "Filthy Fifteen" list of objectionable songs.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-PMRC-10)
After disbanding in 1985 due to musical differences, four out of the five members of Mercyful Fate reunited in 1992 and recorded the album _In the Shadows_, which was released the following year. During the 1990s, the band released four more studio albums and went through several line-up changes. Mercyful Fate went on hiatus in 1999, but had reunited on occasion during the 2000s. On August 1, 2019, it was announced that Mercyful Fate was reuniting on a more permanent basis, with plans to tour[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-shermann_bio-2)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-11) and release a new album, which will be their first since _9_ in 1999.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Blabbermouth_album-12)

The staff of _Loudwire_ named Mercyful Fate the 35th best metal band of all time.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-13)

### Formation and first releases (1981–1985)
[edit]
Mercyful Fate was originally formed in Copenhagen in the spring of 1981,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-14) following the dissolution of the band Brats.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Allmusic-15) Brats were a punk/metal band featuring future Mercyful Fate members King Diamond and guitarists Hank Shermann and Michael Denner.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Interview-16) After two studio albums and several line-up changes (including the addition of Diamond and the departure of Denner), Diamond and Shermann began writing new material that was much heavier than any of Brats' previous work.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Interview-16) The band's record label CBS was not pleased with the material, and demanded they stop singing in English and become more commercial.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Interview-16) As a result, Diamond and Shermann quit the group and went on to form Mercyful Fate.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Interview-16) Former Rock Nalle bassist Ole Beich (later of L.A.

### Formation and first releases (1981–1985)

### Formation and first releases (1981–1985)
In July 1983, Mercyful Fate recorded their debut album at Easy Sound Recording in Copenhagen.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Melissa-21) Entitled _Melissa_, the album was produced by Henrik Lund and released in October 1983 through Roadrunner Records.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Melissa-21)_Melissa_ has been referred to as "one of the first records to start to develop an 'extreme metal' sound" and was major influence on the then-emerging thrash metal, death metal and black metal genres.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-22) The character of Melissa, a witch who was burned at the stake, appears for the first time on the eponymous debut album and intermittently throughout the band's later work.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-23) One of the album's tracks, "Into the Coven", received particular attention two years later, when it was listed by the Parents Music Resource Center (PMRC) as one of their "Filthy Fifteen" songs due to its perceived occult content.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-PMRC-10) King Diamond was, in reality, interested in LaVeyan Satanism, which he called "a life philosophy" and stated that it had nothing to do with the Devil of Abrahamic religions.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-24) After a number of concerts around Denmark, Mercyful Fate entered the studio in May 1984 to record their second studio album _[Don't Break the Oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Break\_the\_Oath "Don't Break the Oath")_, which was released on September 7, 1984.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Don't_Break_the_Oath-25) During the album's supporting tour,

the band played the US for two months and made festival appearances in Germany.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#1-26) Despite winning a cult following around the world, Mercyful Fate broke up in April 1985, due to musical differences.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Allmusic-15)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#1-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Music_Box-27) Guitarist Hank Shermann wanted the band to move to a more commercial sound;[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Allmusic-15) King Diamond refused and announced his departure from Mercyful Fate, which led to the band breaking up.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#1-26)

### After disbanding (1985–1992)
[edit]
After Mercyful Fate broke up, King Diamond, along with Michael Denner and Timi Hansen, formed the eponymous King Diamond band.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-bandhistory02-28)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#1-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Music_Box-27) Both Denner and Hansen stayed with the group until 1987's _Abigail_, after which both left King Diamond.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-King_Diamond_band_members-29) They were replaced by Mike Moon and Hal Patino, respectively, and King Diamond continued releasing albums even after Mercyful Fate had reformed.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-King_Diamond_band_members-29) After leaving King Diamond, Denner opened up a recordshop in Copenhagen, until 1988, when he formed the band Lavina (which would later become Zoser Mez), along with former bandmate Hank Shermann.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-King_Diamond_band_members-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#2-30)_[better source needed_] Hank Shermann had formed the hard rock band Fate in 1985, after having left Mercyful Fate.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Fate_Allmusic-31) With Fate, Shermann released two albums: 1985's _Fate_ and 1986's _A Matter of Attitude_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Fate_Allmusic-31) After leaving the band,

### After disbanding (1985–1992)
Shermann joined-up with Michael Denner to form Lavina.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Fate_Allmusic-31)
During the time Mercyful Fate were disbanded, Roadrunner Records released three Mercyful Fate compilation albums. _The Beginning_ was released on June 24, 1987, and featured material from the band's 1982 self-titled EP, as well as rare live and studio recordings.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-The_Beginning-32) On May 12, 1992, _Return of the Vampire_ was released, which was another compilation of rare studio recordings.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Return_of_the_Vampire-33) On October 6, 1992, Roadrunner Records released _A Dangerous Meeting_, a greatest hits album under the King Diamond name, featuring material from both Mercyful Fate and King Diamond.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-A_Dangerous_Meeting-34)

### Reunion (1992–1999)

In 1992, King Diamond, Hank Shermann, Michael Denner and Timi Hansen reunited to reform Mercyful Fate (drummer Kim Ruzz was replaced by Morten Nielsen).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) The result was the band's third album _In the Shadows_, which was released on June 22, 1993 through Metal Blade Records.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-In_the_Shadows-35) The album also featured a guest appearance by Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich (a fellow Dane) on the track "Return of the Vampire".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-In_the_Shadows-35) For the album's supporting tour, Morten Nielsen was replaced by King Diamond drummer Snowy Shaw, due to a knee injury Nielsen had sustained.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) Bassist Timi Hansen was also replaced by [Sharlee D'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharlee_D'Angelo "Sharlee D'Angelo"), as Hansen did not want to take part in touring.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-About-36)_[better source needed_] On June 27, 1994, the band released _The Bell Witch_, an EP of live tracks, as well as studio recordings from _In the Shadows_.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-The_Bell_Witch-37)

texts.0:
Mercyful Fate was formed in early 1981 in Copenhagen, Denmark, by vocalist King Diamond and guitar player Hank Shermann. Guitarist Michael Denner, Bassist Timi Hansen and drummer Kim Ruzz soon joined to complete the band line-up.
The band recorded two demos in 1981, and later signed with Rave On Records in Holland, for recording of their successful EP “Mercyful Fate”, released on November 8th 1982. The EP was soon in heavy rotation around the core metal radio stations, starting a new breed in Heavy Metal with their unique sound.
Mercyful Fate signed a new deal with Roadrunner Records in 1983 to make their first full length album “Melissa”, recorded and released that same year. In 1984 the band went back into the studio to record their legendary album “Don’t Break The Oath”, released on September 7th 1984.
Soon after Mercyful Fate started a two month US Tour, which took them across the States several times, including sharing the stage with Motorhead and Exciter for the last part of the tour. The shows had created a brush fire within the metal community, and Mercyful Fate was now getting a lot of recognition. The year of 1984 ended with a 5 days tour in Germany, together with Motorhead, Girlschool, Helix and Talon.
First concert of 1985 was in their hometown of Copenhagen, an old movie theater with higher capacity. The show was sold out, and the band displayed new levels of their stage show. It was a huge success, and was a new highlight for Mercyful Fate.
In April 1985 though, the band decided to part ways, for each to pursue new challenges. The King Diamond band was born and had huge success the following years with five studio album releases on Roadrunner Records. King Diamond has since signed with Metal Blade Records, and is going stronger than ever.
Summer of 1992 Mercyful Fate decided to get back together and penned a new deal with Brian Slagel and his label Metal Blade Records. “In The Shadows” was released in 1993, and was and instant success followed by a sold out US tour.
texts.1:
The following years Mercyful Fate released another five studio albums and toured Europe, US and South America many times. The highlight of the year 1999 was their critically acclaimed “9” album, released on May 25th 1999. It was followed by a European tour with Metallica, where King and Hank several times joined them on stage performing the medley “Mercyful Fate” which Metallica had recorded on their “Garage Inc.” double tribute album, in 1998. A USA tour and touring in South America followed.
Mercyful Fate played 36 concerts in Europe, USA and Mexico in 2022. Two concerts in South America in 2024. Work in progress for a full Album.

texts.1: **Mercyful Fate** is a Danish heavy metal band from Copenhagen, formed in 1981 by vocalist King Diamond and guitarist Hank Shermann.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-shermann_bio-2) Influenced by progressive rock and hard rock, and with lyrics dealing with LaVeyan Satanism (often with ironic or sardonic use of Christian themes) and the occult, Mercyful Fate was part of the first wave of black metal in the early to mid-1980s, along with Venom and Bathory.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-4) The band is also cited as a formative influence to the then-nascent genres of thrash metal[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Kerry_King-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-metalinjection-6) and death metal, as well as the Norwegian black metal scene.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Melissa_Review-9)
texts.2:
Since its inception in 1981, Mercyful Fate has released seven studio albums, two extended plays, and four compilation albums. After several line-up changes and self-made demos, they released their self-titled EP in 1982, with the line-up of King Diamond (vocals), Hank Shermann (lead and rhythm guitars), Michael Denner (rhythm and lead guitars), Timi Hansen (bass), and Kim Ruzz (drums). With this line-up, the group recorded its first two studio albums: 1983's _Melissa_ and 1984's _[Don't Break the Oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Break\_the\_Oath "Don't Break the Oath")_. In spite of their reputation as one of the most acclaimed bands of the European heavy metal scene of the 1980s, Mercyful Fate was the subject of controversy due to their satanic imagery, and one of their songs "Into the Coven" (from _Melissa_) later gained notoriety for appearing as one of the PMRC's "Filthy Fifteen" list of objectionable songs.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-PMRC-10)
After disbanding in 1985 due to musical differences, four out of the five members of Mercyful Fate reunited in 1992 and recorded the album _In the Shadows_, which was released the following year. During the 1990s, the band released four more studio albums and went through several line-up changes. Mercyful Fate went on hiatus in 1999, but had reunited on occasion during the 2000s. On August 1, 2019, it was announced that Mercyful Fate was reuniting on a more permanent basis, with plans to tour[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-shermann_bio-2)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-11) and release a new album, which will be their first since _9_ in 1999.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Blabbermouth_album-12)

[edit]

During the time Mercyful Fate were disbanded, Roadrunner Records released three Mercyful Fate compilation albums. _The Beginning_ was released on June 24, 1987, and featured material from the band's 1982 self-titled EP, as well as rare live and studio recordings.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-The_Beginning-32) On May 12, 1992, _Return of the Vampire_ was released, which was another compilation of rare studio recordings.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Return_of_the_Vampire-33) On October 6, 1992, Roadrunner Records released _A Dangerous Meeting_, a greatest hits album under the King Diamond name, featuring material from both Mercyful Fate and King Diamond.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-A_Dangerous_Meeting-34)

### Reunion (1992–1999)
[edit]
In 1992, King Diamond, Hank Shermann, Michael Denner and Timi Hansen reunited to reform Mercyful Fate (drummer Kim Ruzz was replaced by Morten Nielsen).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) The result was the band's third album _In the Shadows_, which was released on June 22, 1993 through Metal Blade Records.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-In_the_Shadows-35) The album also featured a guest appearance by Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich (a fellow Dane) on the track "Return of the Vampire".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-In_the_Shadows-35) For the album's supporting tour, Morten Nielsen was replaced by King Diamond drummer Snowy Shaw, due to a knee injury Nielsen had sustained.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) Bassist Timi Hansen was also replaced by [Sharlee D'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharlee_D'Angelo "Sharlee D'Angelo"), as Hansen did not want to take part in touring.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-About-36)_[better source needed_] On June 27, 1994, the band released _The Bell Witch_, an EP of live tracks, as well as studio recordings from _In the Shadows_.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-The_Bell_Witch-37)
